items.summary:
The South Carolina case that shocked the country — an 11-month-old baby buried alive in a dog crate for roughly 24 hours — has put his father, Michael Comer , at the center of an attempted murder investigation in Lexington County.  

Comer’s arrest in Batesburg-Leesville, South Carolina, the dramatic rescue of baby Koah Sharp and the child’s custody situation that reportedly preceded the incident have drawn national attention to a case authorities say could have ended in tragedy if not for a search party that spotted freshly disturbed dirt. 

Here’s what to know about Comer, the charges against him and the family at the heart of the case. 

Michael Comer’s Charges and Arrest in Lexington County 
 Michael Comer is c harged with attempted murder , unlawful conduct toward a child, custodial interference and burglary, according to court records.  

Dad Allegedly Killed Infant, Took Baby to Hospital With 'Severe' Injuries 

The Lexington County Sheriff’s Department says Comer took his 11-month-old son, Koah, while the boy was in the care of Comer’s mother on November 9, 2026, triggering an urgent search near Batesburg-Leesville.  

Comer was found later that evening at a local outbuilding — without Koah — and was initially taken into custody on a burglary charge. 

He was denied bond days later on November 12.  

According to Tyler Douglas , the lead investigator with the Lexington County Sheriff’s Department, Comer showed no remorse for the attempted murder of his son while appearing before a judge, the Associated Press and CBS News reported.

items.title: Man Killed Estranged Wife in Murder-Suicide, Prompting Lockdowns at Schools
items.summary:
Authorities in Iowa said that a man fatally shot his estranged wife before he took his own life in an apparent murder-suicide, which prompted nearby schools to go into a precautionary lockdown.

Emmet County 911 Dispatch received a call on Friday, November 13, reporting that two gunshots were heard around 2:03 p.m. near the Good Samaritan Center in Estherville, Iowa, according to Northwest Iowa Now .

Dispatchers received another call around the same time reporting that an unresponsive woman had been found bleeding in a driveway.

Estherville Police Department officers and the Estherville Ambulance then responded to a nearby home and determined that the victim, Rhonda Oleson , had died from her injuries.

Estranged Husband Kills Wife Before Dying By Suicide in Murder-Suicide 

Following a brief investigation, officials determined that the victim, 57, had been shot by her estranged husband, Greg Oleson , and authorities set out on a search for the suspect.

The nearby Estherville Lincoln Central Schools and the Good Samaritan Center were placed on precautionary lockdowns to make sure that students, staff, residents and visitors remained safe as officers looked for Greg, 58, who fled to a rural area.

Authorities used investigative technology to locate Greg’s vehicle in Emmet County. As officers approached his vehicle, they found him deceased after he apparently died by suicide.

Officers eventually determined that there was no threat to the public, and the lockdowns were lifted.

It’s not currently clear what evidence authorities found to name Greg as the suspect in the…

items.title: Anne Hathaway and Husband Adam Shulman’s Relationship Timeline
items.summary:
Anne Hathaway  met husband   Adam Shulman  and it was love at first sight — but their real-life fairy tale almost didn’t come true.

“You know when you don’t know someone very well, you just meet them and you’re like, ‘Wow, you really have it going on?’… We hit it off immediately, but it took us a pretty long time to get together,” Hathaway told   Vogue  in October 2010, noting that despite the terrible timing, she was convinced she had found The One.

The pair first crossed paths through mutual friends while attending the Palm Springs Film Festival in April 2008. While the  Ella Enchanted  actress told   Harper’s Bazaar UK   in February 2013 that she knew “from the second I met him that he was the love of my life,” she “also knew that I couldn’t have met him at a worse time.”

Hathaway ultimately took a chance on Shulman — and she hasn’t looked back since.

The pair went on to get engaged in 2011 and tie the knot one year later. Since their nuptials, the couple have welcomed sons Jonathan and Jack, who were born in 2016 and 2019, and a third baby born in fall 2026.

items.title: Cause of Sports Broadcaster Dan Hicks' Sudden Death at 64 Revealed
items.summary:
A cause of death has been revealed for legendary NBC Sports broadcaster Dan Hicks following his sudden death on Wednesday, November 11 .  

Hicks’ immediate cause of death was multifocal pneumonia, according to a death certificate obtained by The California Post . He was 64.  

He was pronounced dead at 5:32 p.m. on Wednesday at a hospital in Greenwich, Connecticut.  

The certificate stated that Hicks had also been dealing with a pulmonary edema (caused by fluid buildup in the lungs) that was preceded by an upper respiratory infection. He also had autoimmune hemolytic anemia, described by the Cleveland Clinic as “a rare condition where the immune system mistakenly produces antibodies that attack and destroy the body’s red blood cells faster than the bone marrow can replace them.” 

Boxer Lee Reeves Dead at 31 After Suffering Brain Injury During Fight 

The broadcaster’s longtime wife, ESPN anchor Hannah Storm , announced his death on social media last week.  

“He was a devoted husband of over 30 years, loving father to our three daughters, and cherished friend to so many,” Storm shared via Instagram on Thursday, November 12. “His loss is immeasurable.” 

Hicks and Storm shared daughters Hannah , 29, Ellery , 28, and Riley , 25. 

“Dan was truly one of a kind and, quite simply, the person everyone wanted to be around,” Storm said. “When he walked into the room, he brought the energy, the laughter, and the people together. He was endlessly kind, thoughtful and funny, and he made everyone feel like they mattered. Our three daughters and I are heartbroken. We are grateful…
items.t: Cause of Sports Broadcaster Dan Hicks' Sudden Death at 64 Revealed

items.title: Brothers Sentenced for Torturing and Killing Family of 4, Setting Home Ablaze
items.summary:
Two brothers will spend the rest of their lives in prison for torturing and killing a family of four inside their upstate New York home.

Julio and Luis Soriano received life sentences without parole on Monday, November 16, after they were convicted of murdering their cousin Fraime Ubaldo, his girlfriend and the couple’s two young children at their Monroe County home in 2024, Spectrum News reported.

“A family was tortured and murdered,” Monroe County District Attorney Brian Green said in a Monday statement on the case prosecuted by Wayne County prosecutors.

items.title: I saw how brightly stars like Russell Brand could shine, but there is darkness in the shadows | Sophie Heawood
items.summary:
After years of celebrity interviews, I have learned not to be fooled by the allure of fame. We never really know them – we know what they want us to know

As I sat in Southwark crown court, listening to the final day of Russell Brand’s trial, there was one subject that came up repeatedly, invoked as often by his defence as the prosecution. I don’t mean sex or coercion, but fame. It ran through every victim impact statement and loomed so large in the courtroom that it felt as if it was almost on trial itself.

I’m an entertainment journalist who has been covering celebrities for more than 20 years – as long as Brand has been one – and I have written about him at various stages of his career. But I went to Southwark crown court as a member of the public who wanted to see justice done. For the women he had hurt, for the ones who couldn’t get as far as the courtroom, and for all of us who came of age at a time when rape culture was so fast and furious that young women mistook it for a joke that we were in on. In the age of lads’ mags, sex felt cheapened, yet somehow we were the ones who ended up paying for this. So it was doubly strange to sit in court and feel somehow complicit in it - in how this media culture had encouraged Russell Brand.

Continue reading...
items.t: I saw how brightly stars like Russell Brand could shine, but there is darkness in the shadows | Sophie Heawood

He sees the dozens of cameras and journalists lined outside Southwark crown court, many of whom have been waiting since before 7am, and he tells himself that the media are all against him. “It seems to me that they believe that I am guilty, and that this should be the rubber-stamping of the process of my destruction.”

He walks with his wife, Laura, and his bodyguard past the photographers, “clickering, clackering, snickering paparazzi, like locusts, peculiar concoctions, not fully humans”, and up into the court, where he is suddenly overwhelmed by “the presence of something very beautiful, grace”. “In a situation like I’m in, it’s impossible not to turn to God. Truth and justice are the only things that can save me,” he thinks.
